gen-dafont-pixel-operator-fs-technor: Fixed-width terminal letters make Pixel Operator read as solid blocks, never skylines. Technor follows in a glowing neon-tube line with barely any gap between cases, and its wide bowls keep a longer passage cool and smooth, a plain sans with a geometric hum.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-fs-gambetta: Plakkaat hits heavy, its terminals curling round to nearly touch the stem, all drawn with one fixed nib. Gambetta, a text serif with gently shifting stroke weight, would let that heavy heading shrink into timidity if the heading were made small.
gen-dafont-plakkaat-lora: Terminals that sweep round to nearly touch the stem give Plakkaat its bent-straw, heavy look. And Lora, a classic serif with a broad-mouthed c and slight hairline thinning on its curves, can take a generous body size without losing its bookish manner.
gen-dafont-prime-fs-hind: Hind goes first, a sans-serif drawn like a string pulled taut. Prime has gentle swelling on its curves and closed, bulky letters that carry the personality, while Hind keeps its c open and its lowercase nearly the height of the capitals for the quiet work.
gen-dafont-quantum-lora: Loose, spacious and tech-clean, Quantum keeps its mouths open and its ascenders short. And Lora, a serif with modest hairline thinning at the curves, settles in under it with a literary feel, so the page moves from sleek display to bookish text.
gen-dafont-quantum-noto-serif: Quantum has no hairlines anywhere in its alphabet, just loose letterfit and open mouths. Noto Serif, a text serif with a prominent x-height and a subtle thick-and-thin cadence, carries a longer passage with a literary, unhurried rhythm.
gen-dafont-quark-fs-hind: Quark draws contrast-free strokes with a spacious c, so the middle zone dominates its line. But Hind, a plain sans of nearly matching capitals and lowercase, takes over the steady reading work, while Quark handles the geometric, technical headline.
gen-dafont-radikal-fs-hind: Bold and professional, Radikal bends its s like wire and leaves a generous gap after every glyph. Hind, a sans with open c endings, does the quieter reading.
gen-dafont-reckoner-fs-sentient: Sentient arrives sophisticated and contemporary, with pinched apertures and crossbars a touch thinner than the stems. Reckoner, clean and clamped tight, traces its single thick thread above it, a level beat against the text serif's arches that thin as they leave the stem.
gen-dafont-redux-lora: Wide-spaced and geometric, Redux enters each curve with a big visible stroke. Lora, a text serif with modest hairline thinning and a welcoming c, steps in below to give that open display a bookish voice.
